name: Fade Up Characters
description: A pill label lifts in, then each letter of the headline rises 70% of its height and fades on in a fast left-to-right ripple.
move: A pill label lifts in, then each letter of the headline rises 70% of its height and fades on in a fast left-to-right ripple.
how: Characters split inside unbreakable word spans. yPercent 70→0 over 1.0s, stagger 0.028, ease cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); opacity 0→1 over 0.45s with the same stagger. Exit at 3.3s: yPercent -55 and fade, stagger 0.016, power2.in.
adapt: Use for short headlines (under ~30 characters); longer lines should lower the stagger so the ripple stays under ~0.8s. Placeholder copy is generic; replace it with the product's words. Colours come from the palette tokens at the top of the page (--bg, --surface, --ink, --muted, --accent, --accent-2); change those to re-brand it.
port: All motion is inline in index.html. GSAP pages: register the CustomEase curves, scope selectors to the shot element and rebuild the same timeline; the split helper is inline and dependency-free.
caveats: Original implementation of the After Effects "Fade Up Characters" idea; no AE preset files, expressions or numbers are copied and fidelity to a specific AE render is not claimed.
Starts and ends on an empty stage so it loops cleanly; trim the exit when the next shot cuts in.
